summary.prose: Build the shared terminal installer foundation: exact private runtime/bootstrap assets, immutable bounded bundle delivery, one OS-locked controller, explicit owning-peer contracts and readiness-gated installed TUI handoff. Revision 2 preserves all eight task identities, dependencies, implementation scope, acceptance checks and t1-t7 tests; only t8 test requirements and this explanation change, adding the actual successor launcher regression. Per approved LLD sections 3.5 and 7, S1 validates deterministic peer/TUI fixtures, actual produced ZIP/native-load probes and host POSIX PTY smoke with PowerShell source checks; the three live-strategy coverage rows identify prerequisite S1 tasks rather than completed live qualification. Actual enabled-target clean install/successor upgrade with exact IPC readiness, real migration-failure startup blocking/TUI exit behavior, and native Windows PowerShell terminal execution remain mandatory after s3/s4/s5 integration in S8 before their targets are enabled; no fixture result qualifies a production release or platform.

tasks.title: Define installer contracts and installation location resolution
tasks.summary: Create foundation-owned strict schemas/types for sc1/sc2/sc3/sc5/sc6/sc7, including approved escalation and bridge handshake/control envelopes. Implement the pure explicit-home/endpoint resolver and release-policy validation; do not wire daemon boot or IDE transports.
acceptanceChecks: Validate untrusted manifests, entrypoint/module containment, unique ordered hook identities, version/target/predecessor identity and bounded protocol records; reject unknown/incompatible input before execution.
Resolve one stable installation/user-scoped endpoint from default or explicit absolute home; reject unsupported/network/symlinked controller roots and overlong socket paths without truncation.
Keep current application IPC payloads intact; define dependency/bridge/hook contracts without implementing s3/s4/s5/s7 behavior.

tests.name: strict installer schemas reject invalid target runtime entrypoint hook and bridge records
explicit home endpoint and terminal launch identity remain consistent
correlated bridge send cancel write outcomes preserve uncertainty
bridge hello ready requires exact nonce within three seconds before dispatch

tasks.title: Implement native operation locking and atomic controller storage
tasks.summary: Add the minimal release-built Node-API v8 platform binding for non-inheritable flock/LockFileEx handles, platform atomic replacement and user-SID lookup. Implement versioned single-writer controller snapshots and read-only missing/corrupt inspection.
acceptanceChecks: Mutations require one OS-held lock; never rename/unlink operation.lock, inspect PIDs, steal by age or create a heartbeat ownership protocol.
Atomically replace and durably flush snapshots through qualified platform adapters; active release and operation publish together with revision checks.
Native addons are built on release/development machines, packaged per target and never compiled on a bundle consumer; unavailable target qualification remains explicit.

Implement each declared platform adapter; execute host-native exclusion/self-exit/atomic-replace crash checks and record other-target smoke as qualified or unavailable. Enforce per-target publication gating while s8 retains live E2E evidence ownership.

tests.name: OS lock excludes another writer and releases on owned fixture self exit
atomic replacement crash points preserve one valid snapshot
target private runtime loads qualified native lock and atomic adapters

tasks.title: Publish pinned private-runtime bootstrap assets
tasks.summary: Create canonical scripts/install.sh and scripts/install.ps1 plus release-owned Node 22.22.1/matching npm policy. Implement download/hash/staged extraction of exact official runtime assets and separately digest-bound bootstrap/native control assets without host Node.
acceptanceChecks: Use independently verified official per-target archive hashes and absolute private executables; reject missing prerequisites, corrupt/wrong-target runtime and Node injection variables without elevation or PATH-runtime fallback.
Stage/publish runtime and control assets without overwriting running operation code; use matching npm-cli.js through private Node only on build/dev machines.
No global PATH edit, system service, execution-policy bypass, signing claim or end-user npm/compiler requirement; preserve explicit CUDA-install environment value and default skip only when absent.

tests.name: bootstrap rejects corrupt wrong target runtime and missing extraction prerequisites
bootstrap works with missing or wrong host Node and clears Node injection
private runtime policy matches native headers and preserves explicit CUDA setting

tasks.title: Build target-specific bundle and canonical installer release assets
tasks.summary: Create scripts/package-installer.mjs and coordinated publishing integration. Emit release.json sidecar, immutable inventory/ZIP, production dependency closure, built daemon/TUI/assets, release-built native lock binding, official runtime archive and single-file dependency-minimal manager/installer bootstrap.
acceptanceChecks: Exact source revision/target/runtime/protocol/compatibility and file inventory are bound to independent sidecar archive digests; no hash contains its own bytes.

Use pinned explicit ZIP-reader/bundling dependencies and existing build coordination; preserve native optional dependency closure, safely dereference only verified in-root links and retain daemon/TUI resources.
Emit identical manual/VS Code/JetBrains script version/hash/bytes via existing resource-copy boundary without implementing native IDE terminal APIs or restoring retired names.
Run representative native/runtime payload probes before advertising a target; unavailable targets remain unqualified and cannot be published as supported.

Early publisher tests use explicitly labeled controlled payload fixtures only. Production packaging rejects absent real manager/installer/daemon/TUI entrypoints; final actual payload assembly occurs after t6/t8 implementation.

tests.name: publisher binds exact source target runtime inventory and independent archive digest
production payload closure rejects missing entrypoints and escaping workspace links
bundled manager excludes DB indexer model imports and consumer npm build
published manual and both IDE installer script assets have exact byte parity

tasks.title: Prepare immutable bundle candidates with bounded safe extraction
tasks.summary: Implement bundle delivery resolution/download, sidecar/schema/inventory checks and streaming bounded ZIP staging/publication using the approved yauzl reader. Return the common prepared candidate without selecting or starting it.
acceptanceChecks: Reject traversal/drive/UNC/ADS/backslash ambiguities, symlinks/special files, duplicates/case collisions, encryption/unsupported entries and entry/byte/ratio/size violations before unsafe execution/publication.
Check all runtime/target/predecessor/entrypoint and inventory identities; never run npm/build on consumers or silently switch bundle to dev.
Download/cancel/build-input failures clean only owned staging and preserve incumbent selection/data/running intent; retry revalidates the exact immutable candidate.

tests.name: hostile ZIP corpus cannot escape staging or exceed bounded extraction
download digest target runtime cancellation and retry preserve incumbent

tasks.title: Implement the manager operation controller and required peer admission
tasks.summary: Implement inspect/check-upgrade and serialized mutation state transitions over the controller snapshot. Define required sibling capability ports and durable candidate/admission metadata; use deterministic peers to exercise handoffs without implementing their owned behavior.
acceptanceChecks: Ordinary manager rejects install even with a forged source/bootstrap marker; interactive installation has a separate TTY-only entrypoint.
Before disruption require actual dependency, lifecycle/readiness and migration ports; missing capability is capability-unavailable, never fixture/no-op production success.

Own controller.json exclusively; candidate owns hook journal and wrapper owns migration receipt. Persist operation/session/nonce/receipt-path admission before spawn and consume s4/s5 evidence through ports.

Keep uncertain quiescing/migration/activation blocked; exact-offer acceptance, candidate compatibility, revision checks and explicit same-candidate recovery prohibit automatic predecessor restart, guessed exit or duplicate runners.

tests.name: install is rejected even with a forged source/bootstrap marker
required peer admission and exact offer state transitions fail closed
manager death and candidate journal receipt projections cannot start duplicate runner
corrupt controller revisions and immutable candidate mismatches fail closed

tasks.title: Route same-operation immediate escalation to the lock owner
tasks.summary: Implement the approved sc2 escalation forwarding/control lane within the short-lived manager. Preserve ordinary mutation exclusion while allowing an explicit same-operation immediate message to reach the live lock owner during drain.
acceptanceChecks: Use protected installation/operation/owner-session-bound endpoint discovery and same-user authorization; stale/wrong-phase/wrong-identity requests fail.

Owner remains responsive while waiting; duplicate/cross-window immediate intent coalesces and uses the original s4 instance/completion endpoint/nonce. Forwarder never mutates snapshots or steals/releases the owner lock.
Absent owner returns escalation-unavailable/uncertain and requires explicit reconciled recovery; never use PID/kill/signal fallback, timer-based escalation or competing replacement.

tests.name: cross window immediate forwards while owner lock remains held
duplicate stale wrong phase and dead owner escalation preserve exact completion nonce

tasks.title: Complete terminal-owned installation and installed TUI handoff
tasks.summary: Compose canonical scripts, private runtime, bundle preparation and required peer ports into the interactive terminal installer. Publish the installed launcher selecting a complete immutable manager/runtime pair and perform the ready-to-TUI foreground handoff.
acceptanceChecks: TTY stdin/stdout/stderr own mode/source selection, exact dependency consent, progress/errors and recommendations; never accept IDE-filled consent or a direct IDE install request.
Only validated exact-ready completion may commit ready, release mutation lock and start installed TUI in the same terminal using private runtime; TUI exit leaves daemon running and returns shell.
Failure/cancel never launches TUI; post-success TUI launch error retains completed install and prints the exact retry command without reinstall/rollback.

Cross-window busy/duplicate/terminal-close cases preserve one operation and no automatic relaunch. Keep source scripts/insrc distinct from the installed launcher and keep the host v2 daemon untouched.
Dev selection only captures validated delivery and requires the s2 adapter; absent dev/dependency/lifecycle/migration capability fails explicitly without invented sibling behavior.
After all s1 entrypoints land, assemble/probe the actual complete payload through t4 tooling. Fixture results remain labeled and no production E2E/install or unqualified-platform success is inferred.

tests.name: terminal installer requires all TTY streams and absent dev adapter fails explicitly
ready commit and lock release precede same terminal installed TUI
cancel install failure and post install TUI error preserve correct outcome
assemble actual complete foundation payload only after all entrypoints exist
successor upgrade replaces its owned launcher and preserves ready selection
canonical POSIX terminal script preserves I O and fixture TUI handoff and PowerShell source preserves invocation contract

testStrategyCoverage.lldStrategyItem: Strict manifest/runtime/entrypoint/hook validation; unrelated design-corpus ReleaseManifest is not imported.
Manager JSON install is rejected even with a forged source/bootstrap marker; non-TTY interactive entry is rejected.
Explicit home/endpoint and terminal launch schema preserve operation/release identity.
Immutable safe ZIP preparation and inventory verification, including ZIP traversal/ADS/case collision/symlink/oversize/truncation attacks.
Native lock exclusion/release and atomic-replace crash points with fixture processes that self-exit on control input.
Prepare/peer-quiesce/peer-migrate/peer-ready transitions; missing capabilities, uncertainty and first-data-write failures remain blocked.
Complete state and release lock before TUI fixture enters foreground; TUI fixture exit/failure leaves ready installation and peer daemon alive.
Cross-window immediate forwarding while lock stays held: duplicates, stale endpoint, owner death and same completion nonce.
Manager self-exit at journal crash points; live candidate completion; held/unknown lease; stale session/revision; no duplicate hook runs.
Correlated protocol-2 send/cancel/write-boundary contract fixtures; actual Windows binding belongs to s7.
Protocol-2 hello/ready with exact nonce, three-second deadline, no application send before ready, old-helper/malformed/duplicate/early frame failures.
Exact Node version/architecture and native lock addon under each target's shipped runtime.
Shared POSIX/PowerShell scripts preserve direct TTY I/O, report failure/cancel and successful same-terminal TUI handoff.
Bundled manager has no application DB/index/model imports; bundle consumer performs no npm/source build.
Clean install and successor upgrade with actual bundle/native dependencies and IPC readiness on every enabled target.
Both IDE scripts have exact byte parity with manual release script; terminal frontend integration belongs to s6/s7.
Migration refusal/failure blocks actual startup and upgrade; real TUI uses selected daemon and exits without stopping it.
